findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as argv to prevent command injection
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax, `exec` evaluates it rather than passing it only to Git; for example, `topic;id` runs `id` after `git show topic`. Semicolons are valid in Git ref names, and the exported function accepts an unrestricted string, so this also breaks legitimate refs. Keep the branch as a separate argv element with `execFile`.

findings.title: [P2] Avoid the intermediary shell to preserve cancellation
findings.body: For a slow or large `git show`, callers killing the returned child now target the shell created by `exec`, not Git itself. The Git process can continue after the shell exits and retain inherited pipes, whereas the prior `execFile` return value represented Git directly. Use direct argument-based execution so cancellation retains its previous behavior.
